claims.text: The as-synthesized AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are near-equiatomic.
The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are supported on a TEM grid.
In situ heating in an aberration-corrected STEM can investigate the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at atomic resolution.
Real-time atomic-resolution imaging can track lattice and morphological evolution during heating.
EDS mapping or EELS can track the elemental distribution during in situ heating.
Heating induces local elemental rearrangements and diffusion processes at the atomic scale.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the near-equiatomic distribution of Au, Co, Cu, Ni, and Pt.
Configurational-entropy stabilization mitigates thermally driven phase segregation.
Heated AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will retain a homogeneous elemental distribution through the tested temperature range.
The nanoparticles will exhibit minimal structural segregation at elevated temperatures up to approximately 700 °C.
The nanoparticles will undergo minimal morphological change over the tested thermal range.
The nanoparticles will undergo minimal compositional change over the tested thermal range.
At temperatures above approximately 700 °C, segregation or phase changes may become significant.
Reactive environments may promote significant segregation or phase changes.
Observation of distinct phase segregation or substantial structural rearrangement at or below 700 °C would falsify the proposed high-entropy stabilization.
